body.p: One human was wandering. While wandering, he found traces of [other] people. He wandered along their traces. He found a camp. Near them he made [his] camp. In the morning those ogres began to woo the man's younger sister. The ogres wooed [her] and took the man's younger sister. The ogres paid one of their girls for the man's younger sister. The man took their sister, he wandered off with the woman. The ogres wandered off, too. Having sat his son's wife onto the sledge, one old ogre was pulling his daughter-in-law. The daughter-in-law said: "Why are you pulling me?" "Why should you suffer going by foot, child". The old man killed a fat reindeer for the daughter-in-law for eating, he built a yurt separately for her. Then the ogres started shamanizing. In the evening, when the daughter-in-law was alone in her yurt, two girls came to their sister-in-law. "Sister-in-law", they said, "I'll play 'knucklebones' with your hand". The other one said: "I'll play 'knucklebones' with this [hand]". The woman said: "What will be with me, if you play 'knucklebone' with my [finger] bones?" "You'll be sacrificed by the father." There the woman got afraid, she hid her shoes and a knife. Some time passed, their shaman said that two men with two spears should stand opposite [to each other] and watch, in order to spear her well, when she comes. Then the shaman said: "Bring the woman!" The woman stood up, being standing a bit she said: "I want to go out, let me go out!" "It won't be bad if she goes (?); watch, girls". The girls started watching the woman. [DCh]: The first clause is unclear, and the translation does not seem to fit. The woman went out, she said to the girls: "Bring a flint". The girls came, the woman tore off beads from her coat and gave them to the girls. The girls were happy and ran into their yurts. The woman quickly put her coat on the pole, quickly she grabbed her skis and tried to escape. Running along the way, she saw a bent tree beneath the path, she put the skis under the snow and climbed onto the top of the bent tree. Then she started listening. The shaman said: "Well, go after her, something has cracked". The men went off, [there] is only the coat. They began to search, they were searching with kindlings. The woman saw from the tree that they were approaching, she jumped into the snow. She crwaled deeply under the snow. The ogres couldn't find her, they didn't find the woman. They came home and said to the shaman: "We didn't find her". The shaman said: "How shall it be good now? It will be terrible without blood". They sacrificed one of the girls instead of the woman, they started shamanizing. She found the elder brother's way, she went along that way. She was going and going and she reached her elder brother. She went in to the elder brother, crying she said: "You gave me to such people. When they were about to kill me, I just escaped." The woman's brother killed his wife, he put on his sister's clothes, he flayed her [=of his wife] face, he went to the middle of the[StN]: Vasilevich 1958: dÉwjÉ 'stratched' (adj) path and spanned it on a tree, he said to the sister: "Wander to the halt". The sister wandered off. The brother said to the sister: "I will watch here those, who are chasing [you]. If I don't come, say [DCh]: Maybe [that] I was killed". The brother started watching. When it turned noon, those one were filing, they came. "waËmÅan" is a misprint instead of "waËmnan". They started looking at the killed one and said: "Man, how clever, why didn't you run away?" They chopped the killed woman in order to eat her. They lit a bonfire, they started spit-roasting her. The old father cut off her heart and started eating, he said: "Something moves my heart, isn't she one of us?" The others said: "Stop boasting and lying". The ogres started chatting: "Do we chase [him]?" "It would be good", some of them said. "Why should one chase such a clever man, he shall go." The ogres came home. The man went along the traces of his sister, he was going the whole night, he met his sister.
